analysis.title: GS Consumer | Morning Trading Update (US)
key_insights: US futures stabilizing Monday pre-market: SPX +60bps, NDX +40bps, RTY +1.4%, UST 10yr -1bp at 4.85%, WTI -2.75% at $88.30. This follows GS's prime book seeing its largest gross cut since Covid and biggest net cut since Liberation Day last week.
Trump called extensive Iran strikes "highly unlikely," conditional on a "very strong agreement." NVDA is -5% pre-market on a board investigation tied to CEO Huang headlines.
Week ahead: S&P implied move is 2.29% through Friday. Focus is Tuesday CPI (GIR forecasts +16bps core MoM), Fed speakers, and Neocloud earnings from CRWV (Tuesday) and NBIS (Thursday).
FERG beat on top and bottom line and raised the FY guide. Adj. EPS $3.43 vs $3.31 consensus, revenue $9.03B vs $8.74B consensus, organic growth 7.0% vs 4.5% consensus (non-resi +15%, resi +6%).
SGI is -3% on its 4th straight top-line miss vs consensus. 3Q EPS was $1.04 vs $1.05 consensus, and the top end of the FY EPS guide was lowered to $2.85-$2.95 from $2.85-$3.15.
DOLE is -8% on an EPS miss and guide cut. Adj. EPS $0.16 vs $0.32 consensus, FY26 adj. EBITDA guide cut to $380-390M from ~$400M, including a ~$16M European fuel headwind.
DKNG is -2% again after multiple downgrades (Stifel, UBS, JPMorgan) following last week's guidance reset.

Consumer context: over 75% of consumer stocks finished lower Thursday and Friday but the group outperformed on the week given the election rally. On the month staples are +12% and discretionary +16% vs S&P 500. GS desk sees underweight positioning as a continuing tailwind and expects sector buyers (especially in discretionary) to keep re-weighting unless AI/tech sees a major one-way resurgence.

GS Research (Bonnie Herzog) reiterates Buy on EL after a China trip, citing faster China-led innovation, an elevated in-store experience, and a more agile value chain. She sees topline acceleration and operating margin expansion ahead.

GS Research (Kate McShane) shared takeaways from AAP, BOBS and COST management meetings, a narrowing DG vs. Family Dollar price gap, mixed October Placer traffic across hardlines, and home furnishings read-throughs from Wayfair and Arhaus earnings.
The GS Baskets team (Lou) is pitching a short Staples basket trade after recent outperformance.

Prime book flows: US equities were modestly net sold this week with the largest single-stock net selling in 4 months. Info Tech was the most net sold global and US sector, with % selling in global Info Tech about on par with the largest net selling weeks on record (since 2016). Hedge funds sold US Industrials at the fastest pace since Covid (Apr 2020). Staples and Health Care were also sold, while Utilities, Real Estate and Financials were the most net bought.

market_movers.rationale: Bonnie Herzog reiterates Buy after a China trip and Capital Markets Event. She sees faster China-led innovation, 1,400 stores by FY30 (vs. 1,150 in FY26), and four China fulfillment centers, with FY30 targets of +MSD organic sales growth and +DD adjusted EPS growth.
Beat on adj. EPS ($3.43 vs $3.31 consensus) and revenue ($9.03B vs $8.74B consensus), and raised FY26 sales growth guide to ~7% and adj. operating margin to 9.6-9.8%.
4th consecutive top-line miss vs consensus, led by Tempur (North America and International) and Mattress Firm. The top end of FY EPS guide was lowered.
Adj. EPS $0.16 vs $0.32 consensus and FY26 adj. EBITDA guide cut to $380-390M vs $398.4M consensus, on higher costs, tariffs and weather.
Downgraded by Stifel, UBS and JPMorgan after last week's guidance reset.
Wells Fargo initiates coverage of CWH.
Wells Fargo initiates at Equal Weight.
Down 5% pre-market on a board investigation tied to CEO Huang headlines.

sector_views.rationale: GS Baskets team (Lou) pitches a short Staples basket. They cite earnings and dividend yield that look unattractive vs. fixed income, insufficient growth, falling earnings revisions, and valuations in the 90th percentile relative to the last year.
The desk says underweight positioning remains a tailwind and expects buyers to keep re-weighting the sector, after a +16% month vs. the S&P 500.
Prime book data shows Info Tech was by far the most net sold sector, with % selling in global Info Tech about on par with the largest net selling weeks on record (since 2016).

earnings_insights: FERG reported (9 Nov): adj. EPS $3.43 vs $3.31 consensus, revenue $9.03B vs $8.74B consensus, adj. EBITDA $1.03B vs $989.6M consensus, adj. operating profit $962M vs $923.3M consensus. Organic growth 7.0% vs 4.5% consensus. Canada sales $405M vs $424.2M consensus. Gross margin 30.9%, down 40 bps.

FERG FY26 guidance raised: sales growth ~7% (vs mid-single digit prior, ~7.5% consensus), adj. operating margin 9.6-9.8% (vs 9.5-9.8% prior), capex ~$425M (vs $375-425M prior, $410.1M consensus), interest expense ~$235M (vs ~$200M prior).

SGI reported 3Q: adj. EPS $1.04 vs $1.05 consensus. Operating income was 150 bps light on a 320 bps top-line miss, the 4th straight revenue miss vs consensus. The miss was in Tempur (NA and International) and Mattress Firm. Margins were largely in line. FY EPS guide is now $2.85-$2.95 vs prior $2.85-$3.15.

DOLE reported: adj. EPS $0.16 vs $0.32 consensus, adj. EBITDA $84.1M vs $94.4M consensus, revenue $2.37B vs $2.37B consensus. Fruit revenue fell 8% on tariffs and weather, and EMEA EBITDA slipped on weakness in the Netherlands and Spain.
DOLE FY26 adj. EBITDA guide cut to $380-390M (vs ~$400M prior and $398.4M consensus), including a ~$16M European fuel headwind. Q4 improvement is now expected at a lower level.
Upcoming: Neocloud earnings from CRWV (Tuesday) and NBIS (Thursday) as earnings season winds down.
